concepts.def: Found between Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn near the Equator.
The Amazon in South America is the world's largest tropical rainforest.
Hot all year ~27 degrees C with rainfall over 2000 mm per year.
Emergent, canopy, understorey and forest floor.
Dense layer ~30 m up containing most species and blocking sunlight.
Rainforests hold over half of all land species despite ~6% of land. 🌳

walkthroughs.body_html:
Tropical rainforests grow in a narrow belt close to the Equator.

This belt lies between the Tropic of Cancer at 23.5 degrees N and the Tropic of Capricorn at 23.5 degrees S.

The Amazon is the largest, covering much of Brazil.

Climate here is hot and wet all year round.

Average temperatures stay near 27 degrees C with little seasonal variation.

Annual rainfall exceeds 2000 mm, often with daily afternoon downpours.

The forest is structured in four layers.

From top to bottom: emergent, canopy, understorey and forest floor.

The canopy blocks most light, so the floor is dark and bare.
